multi-head-self-attention.idea: Scaled dot-product attention allows a model to connect every word in a sentence to every other word at the same time. Multiple attention heads let the system look at relationships from different angles simultaneously.
multi-head-self-attention.why: Before this method, models read text a word at a time in order, often forgetting earlier details in long paragraphs. Multi-head attention captures rich context instantly across long passages.
multi-head-self-attention.example: In the sentence 'The bank approved the loan because it had funds', an attention head links 'it' to 'bank' while another links 'funds' to 'loan'.

mamba-state-space-models.idea: Mamba processes long sequences of data continuously in linear time by updating an internal memory state instead of comparing every word to all past words.
mamba-state-space-models.why: Standard attention models become significantly slower as text length increases because processing cost grows quadratically. Mamba handles very long context windows efficiently without ballooning memory usage.
mamba-state-space-models.example: A smart assistant can read an entire lengthy financial report in a single pass without slowing down on the final pages.

capital-structure-and-modigliani-miller-.idea: Capital structure theory states that in a friction-free market without taxes or bankruptcy costs, a firm's total value remains unchanged whether financed by debt or equity.
capital-structure-and-modigliani-miller-.why: Understanding this baseline helps financial managers focus on real-world market imperfections like tax benefits from debt interest and the risks of insolvency.
capital-structure-and-modigliani-miller-.example: A software business evaluates whether taking a bank loan or issuing new stock slices the corporate pie differently without changing its underlying operating power.

mergers-and-acquisitions-accretion-dilut.idea: An accretion-dilution analysis tests whether buying another company will increase or decrease the combined company's earnings per share after the deal closes.
mergers-and-acquisitions-accretion-dilut.why: Shareholders track deal mechanics and earnings per share closely to evaluate corporate leadership. A deal that shrinks earnings per share can trigger immediate investor skepticism.
mergers-and-acquisitions-accretion-dilut.example: A profitable retailer buys a growing supplier with cash; because the supplier's profits exceed the lost bank interest, earnings per share rise, making the deal accretive.

aristotelian-rhetorical-triangle-ethos-p.idea: Aristotle showed that persuasive communication rests on three pillars: credibility, emotional connection, and logical reasoning.
aristotelian-rhetorical-triangle-ethos-p.why: An argument relying solely on dry data often fails to move people, while pure emotion without logic quickly loses trust. Balancing this rhetorical triangle creates enduring persuasion.
aristotelian-rhetorical-triangle-ethos-p.example: A doctor explaining a vaccine shares medical trials for logic, personal clinical experience for credibility, and a patient story for empathy.

cialdini-principles-of-persuasion.idea: Human decisions are guided by key behavioral shortcuts including reciprocity, scarcity, authority, consistency, liking, and social consensus.
cialdini-principles-of-persuasion.why: People face thousands of daily choices and rely on mental shortcuts to make fast decisions. Understanding these principles of influence helps teams design honest and compelling messages.
cialdini-principles-of-persuasion.example: An online course mentions that only ten seats remain, triggering the scarcity principle to encourage prompt student enrollment.

elaboration-likelihood-model-central-vs-.idea: The elaboration likelihood model explains that people process persuasive messages through two routes: a deep central path focused on facts, or a fast peripheral path guided by surface cues.
elaboration-likelihood-model-central-vs-.why: Audience attention dictates message design. Motivated audiences demand rigorous evidence, while distracted audiences respond primarily to design quality and speaker charm.
elaboration-likelihood-model-central-vs-.example: A car advertisement highlights crash test ratings for analytical buyers while showcasing an attractive celebrity driving along the coast for casual viewers.

entropy-second-law-thermodynamics.idea: Entropy measures the degree of disorder in a physical system. The second law of thermodynamics states that total entropy in an isolated system consistently increases over time.
entropy-second-law-thermodynamics.why: This universal law explains why heat flows from hot objects to cold ones and why time moves in a forward direction.
entropy-second-law-thermodynamics.example: A hot cup of coffee left on a desk cools down as its heat disperses into the cooler surrounding room, without spontaneously reheating.

vision-transformers-vit.idea: Vision Transformers process images by splitting pictures into a grid of small square patches and treating each patch like a word token in text.
vision-transformers-vit.why: Traditional vision models use rigid spatial filters across pixels. Vision transformers learn global relationships across the entire image from the start.
vision-transformers-vit.example: An image of a cat is divided into multiple smaller squares, and the model analyzes how the ear patch relates to the paw patch across the photo.

swin-transformer-shifted-windows.idea: Swin transformers compute self-attention inside small local windows and shift window boundaries across successive layers to allow cross-window communication.
swin-transformer-shifted-windows.why: Calculating attention across every pixel in high-resolution images is too slow. Shifted windows maintain linear computation while connecting distant image regions.
swin-transformer-shifted-windows.example: A camera system inspects an ultra-wide panorama by analyzing local grids first, then shifting grid borders to detect large objects crossing grid lines.

dividend-policy-vs-share-buybacks.idea: Companies return surplus earnings to owners either through regular cash dividends or by buying back and retiring company shares in the open market.
dividend-policy-vs-share-buybacks.why: Dividends provide predictable cash flow to income investors, whereas share buybacks offer capital allocation flexibility and increase remaining owners' percentage stake.
dividend-policy-vs-share-buybacks.example: A mature tech company repurchases outstanding shares, reducing total share count and raising future earnings per share for all remaining shareholders.

monroe-motivated-sequence-persuasive-spe.idea: Monroe's sequence is a five-step speech framework: grab attention, establish a need, satisfy the problem, visualize the positive outcome, and call for action.
monroe-motivated-sequence-persuasive-spe.why: Listeners resist abrupt demands to change behavior. Walking through human psychological stages builds momentum naturally toward commitment.
monroe-motivated-sequence-persuasive-spe.example: A speaker highlights ocean pollution, explains the harm, proposes reusable water bottles, paints a picture of clean beaches, and asks attendees to sign a pledge.

inoculation-theory-building-cognitive-re.idea: Inoculation theory suggests that exposing people to a weakened counter-argument alongside strong rebuttals builds mental immunity against future persuasion attempts.
inoculation-theory-building-cognitive-re.why: Beliefs that are rarely challenged can crumble quickly under intense pressure. Preempting deceptive arguments strengthens personal conviction before opponents strike.
inoculation-theory-building-cognitive-re.example: A public health campaign explains a common myth before refuting it with clear scientific evidence, preparing citizens to spot false claims later.

central-dogma-molecular-biology.idea: The central dogma describes the primary flow of genetic information inside living cells from DNA storage to RNA messengers to functional proteins.
central-dogma-molecular-biology.why: Proteins perform nearly all biological work in living bodies. Understanding this flow explains how genetic code translates into physical traits and diseases.
central-dogma-molecular-biology.example: A cell reads the DNA blueprint for insulin, transcribes it into messenger RNA, and translates that RNA into active insulin proteins.

mixture-of-experts-moe.idea: Sparse Mixture of Experts (MoE) architectures replace dense feed-forward layers with multiple expert sub-networks, routing each token through a top-k gating mechanism.
mixture-of-experts-moe.why: Dense layers waste parameter capacity on tokens that require specialized computation. Sparse routing scales capacity while keeping per-token computation bounded.
mixture-of-experts-moe.example: Imagine a team of routing algorithms sending coding tokens to math experts during language generation.

rotary-positional-embeddings-rope.idea: Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) encode token locations by rotating query and key representations using orthogonal rotation matrices in paired dimensions.
rotary-positional-embeddings-rope.why: Absolute position vectors degrade when sequence context expands past pre-training boundaries. Relative vector rotations enable attention layers to extrapolate across extended contexts smoothly.
rotary-positional-embeddings-rope.example: Attention queries rotate across vector coordinates to determine relative distance between input words during transformer inference.

residual-connections-resnet.idea: Residual connections introduce identity skip paths that let neural layers learn residual functions relative to incoming layer inputs.
residual-connections-resnet.why: Deep networks encounter vanishing gradient signals during backward passes. Adding identity shortcuts preserves gradient flow directly through deep stacks.
residual-connections-resnet.example: ResNet backbones propagate unmodified activations across convolutional stages so deeper image recognition layers learn incremental feature refinements.

sliding-window-and-longformer-attention.idea: Sliding window attention structures replace dense quadratic matrices with localized attention bands and global anchor tokens across input documents.
sliding-window-and-longformer-attention.why: Full self-attention across lengthy sequences incurs quadratic computational overhead. Local window patterns preserve essential neighbor context at linear computational cost.
sliding-window-and-longformer-attention.example: Longformer processors calculate attention within adjacent token bands while routing global summary tokens across entire documents.

grouped-query-attention-gqa.idea: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) groups multiple query heads to share a smaller pool of key-value heads during transformer decoding.
grouped-query-attention-gqa.why: Standard multi-head attention demands extensive memory bandwidth to transfer cached key-value tensors. Sharing heads relieves memory bandwidth pressure without degrading quality.
grouped-query-attention-gqa.example: Llama checkpoints load consolidated key-value tensors across query head groups to accelerate auto-regressive text decoding.

lora-low-rank-adaptation.idea: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) freezes pre-trained foundation weights and injects trainable rank-decomposition matrix pairs into attention and MLP projection layers.
lora-low-rank-adaptation.why: Modifying all weights across large parameter foundations requires vast memory overhead. Decomposing updates into compact low-rank matrices enables efficient fine-tuning.
lora-low-rank-adaptation.example: Parameter-efficient adapters train low-rank matrices on downstream domain instructions while base transformer layers remain frozen.

qlora-quantized-fine-tuning.idea: QLoRA combines 4-bit NormalFloat quantization with low-rank adaptation adapters to enable fine-tuning on constrained GPU memory hardware.
qlora-quantized-fine-tuning.why: Loading large uncompressed parameters consumes available device memory before fine-tuning begins. Quantizing base layers preserves precision while liberating memory for trainable adapter weights.
qlora-quantized-fine-tuning.example: Quantized base models retain 4-bit NormalFloat weights in GPU memory while backpropagation updates low-rank adapters.

direct-preference-optimization-dpo.idea: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) optimizes language models directly on paired preferences using an implicit reward formulation without reinforcement learning.
direct-preference-optimization-dpo.why: Multi-stage reinforcement pipelines require separate reward estimators and unstable policy updates. A closed-form loss optimizes preference likelihood directly through standard cross-entropy.
direct-preference-optimization-dpo.example: Language model trainers minimize DPO loss over winning and losing response pairs to align conversational outputs.

rlhf-proximal-policy-optimization.idea: RLHF aligns language models with human intentions using policy optimization guided by a reward model trained on comparison feedback.
rlhf-proximal-policy-optimization.why: Supervised training mirrors prompt distributions without distinguishing between subtle response qualities. Scalar reinforcement feedback steers model policies toward human preferences.
rlhf-proximal-policy-optimization.example: InstructGPT pipelines update language policies via reinforcement algorithms against reward scores assigned to generated completions.

constitutional-ai-and-rlaif.idea: Constitutional AI scales alignment by evaluating model outputs against explicit natural language principles to guide synthetic critique and revision loops.
constitutional-ai-and-rlaif.why: Gathering continuous human evaluation data introduces severe operational bottlenecks. Principle-driven feedback generates consistent critique data autonomously.
constitutional-ai-and-rlaif.example: Automated critique loops revise responses according to harmlessness rules before models train on the resulting pairs.

kahneman-tversky-optimization-kto.idea: Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO) aligns language models using prospect theory utility functions directly on unpaired binary desirable or undesirable signals.
kahneman-tversky-optimization-kto.why: Curating pairwise preference rankings requires complex data collection. Evaluating individual outputs against reference baselines aligns models using independent feedback signals.
kahneman-tversky-optimization-kto.example: Alignment pipelines assign binary desirable flags to helpful responses to update generation policy parameters directly.

prompt-tuning-and-prefix-tuning.idea: Prefix-Tuning and prompt tuning freeze base model parameters while prepending continuous virtual token vectors to inputs or key-value layers.
prompt-tuning-and-prefix-tuning.why: Generating distinct model checkpoints for diverse tasks demands excessive storage. Modifying small sets of prefix parameters adapts models without parameter duplication.
prompt-tuning-and-prefix-tuning.example: Virtual token prompts prepend continuous prefix representations to transformer activation sequences for task adaptation.

flashattention-tiling-kernel.idea: FlashAttention restructures attention computation using IO-Aware GPU tiling and online softmax scaling to minimize data movement across memory tiers.
flashattention-tiling-kernel.why: Standard attention mechanisms bottleneck on continuous reads and writes between high-bandwidth memory and fast SRAM caches. Tiling preserves intermediate blocks on-chip.
flashattention-tiling-kernel.example: GPU kernels tile key and query blocks in SRAM to compute attention without writing intermediate matrices.

kv-caching-autoregressive-decoding.idea: KV-Caching in autoregressive generation retains computed key and value activations in memory across successive token generation steps.
kv-caching-autoregressive-decoding.why: Recomputing attention across historical context tokens at every step imposes quadratic computational penalties. Storing key-value tensors restricts computation to incoming tokens.
kv-caching-autoregressive-decoding.example: Generation loops retrieve previous key and value activations from memory to calculate attention for incoming tokens.

pagedattention-virtual-memory.idea: PagedAttention applies virtual memory paging principles to manage key-value caches across non-contiguous physical memory blocks in vLLM serving frameworks.
pagedattention-virtual-memory.why: Continuous memory allocations produce fragmented memory waste when sequence lengths fluctuate during serving. Dynamic paging accommodates fluctuating sequence lengths without allocation waste.
pagedattention-virtual-memory.example: Inference servers allocate non-contiguous memory blocks dynamically to store key-value cache tokens during request processing.

speculative-decoding-draft-models.idea: Speculative decoding utilizes a compact draft model to generate candidate tokens that a larger target model verifies simultaneously.
speculative-decoding-draft-models.why: Autoregressive decoding bottlenecks on memory bandwidth during serial token passes. Validating multiple speculative candidates in parallel forward passes amortizes memory latency.
speculative-decoding-draft-models.example: Target transformers evaluate candidate token sequences generated by lightweight draft models in single verification passes.

awq-activation-aware-quantization.idea: Activation-Aware Weight Quantization (AWQ) protects salient weight channels corresponding to prominent activation magnitudes prior to low-bit weight quantization.
awq-activation-aware-quantization.why: Indiscriminate weight quantization degrades model output by truncating critical outlier channels. Shielding sensitive weight coordinates preserves general task accuracy without retraining.
awq-activation-aware-quantization.example: Compression algorithms identify high-magnitude activation channels to scale and protect essential weights during integer quantization.

gptq-post-training-quantization.idea: GPTQ executes accurate post-training quantization by leveraging second-order Hessian error compensation to adjust remaining unquantized weights iteratively.
gptq-post-training-quantization.why: Sequential parameter rounding without error compensation compounds output deviation across deep layers. Compensating remaining weights preserves layer output fidelity during compression.
gptq-post-training-quantization.example: AutoGPTQ routines quantize weight matrices column by column while adjusting subsequent parameters to compensate rounding errors.

continuous-batching-orca.idea: Iteration-level continuous batching schedules transformer workloads at discrete token steps, inserting and retiring sequences dynamically within active batches.
continuous-batching-orca.why: Static request batching leaves processing hardware underutilized when co-scheduled sequences finish at varying times. Continuous iteration scheduling maximizes hardware occupancy.
continuous-batching-orca.example: Serving engines evict finished sequences and inject incoming generation requests into running batches at iteration boundaries.

beam-search-and-top-p-sampling.idea: Nucleus (Top-p) sampling dynamically samples candidate tokens from the smallest set exceeding probability threshold p, while temperature adjusts output probability distributions.
beam-search-and-top-p-sampling.why: Fixed top-k decoding risks admitting implausible tokens during flat distributions or restricting valid choices during sharp distributions. Adaptive thresholds adjust candidate pools dynamically.
beam-search-and-top-p-sampling.example: Decoding routines scale output logits with temperature and filter probability tails exceeding threshold p before sampling.

dense-retrieval-bi-encoders.idea: Dense retrieval with bi-encoder architectures maps queries and passage texts into a continuous embedding space using twin neural encoders.
dense-retrieval-bi-encoders.why: Lexical indexing misses relevant passages when query vocabulary diverges from source documents. Continuous vector spaces capture semantic correspondence beyond literal surface words.
dense-retrieval-bi-encoders.example: Information retrieval pipelines compare query vector embeddings against passage representations using inner product nearest neighbor search.

cross-encoder-reranking.idea: Cross-encoder reranking feeds query-document pairs jointly through full self-attention layers during multi-stage retrieval to capture token-level interactions.
cross-encoder-reranking.why: Bi-encoders encode queries and passages separately, precluding granular cross-token attention. Joint encoding yields accurate relevance scoring for candidate re-ranking stages.
cross-encoder-reranking.example: Second-stage retrieval ranks candidate passages by processing query and text tokens together through cross-encoder attention layers.

hierarchical-navigable-small-world-hnsw.idea: Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graphs organize vectors into hierarchical graph layers to execute approximate nearest neighbor search in logarithmic time.
hierarchical-navigable-small-world-hnsw.why: Exhaustive vector distance scans become computationally prohibitive across massive embedding indexes. Multi-layer graphs allow greedy routing across skip layers toward proximate neighbors.
hierarchical-navigable-small-world-hnsw.example: Vector databases traverse upper graph links to reach relevant clusters before exploring bottom layers for nearest neighbors.

graphrag-knowledge-graph-retrieval.idea: GraphRAG extracts entity-relationship knowledge graphs and community summaries from source text to guide structured context retrieval during query generation.
graphrag-knowledge-graph-retrieval.why: Standard passage search fails to synthesize dispersed concepts that span separate documents. Structured graph edges connect related entities across heterogeneous text corpora.
graphrag-knowledge-graph-retrieval.example: Retrieval pipelines query entity relationship graphs and community summaries to answer broad questions across complex corpora.

hypothetical-document-embeddings-hyde.idea: Hypothetical Document Embeddings (HyDE) prompts a language model to generate hypothetical documents whose embeddings guide zero-shot dense passage retrieval.
hypothetical-document-embeddings-hyde.why: Short or ambiguous search queries lack sufficient lexical context for effective dense vector matching. Synthetic documents mirror the embedding patterns of target source texts.
hypothetical-document-embeddings-hyde.example: Search applications embed generated hypothetical answers to locate relevant real documents within dense index collections.

denoising-diffusion-probabilistic-models.idea: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) generate data samples by learning to reverse a parameterized Markov chain that injects noise into images.
denoising-diffusion-probabilistic-models.why: Direct likelihood modeling often encounters unstable adversarial dynamics during generation. Parameterized reverse denoising steps reconstruct sharp sample distributions stably.
denoising-diffusion-probabilistic-models.example: Image synthesis models predict and remove injected Gaussian noise across iterative steps to generate realistic pixel outputs.

classifier-free-guidance-cfg.idea: Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) steers diffusion generation toward prompt alignment by combining conditional and unconditional sampling predictions without external classifier networks.
classifier-free-guidance-cfg.why: Training external classifiers on noisy intermediate representations introduces architectural complexity. Jointly training with null condition dropouts enables direct guidance scaling.
classifier-free-guidance-cfg.example: Generative diffusion pipelines extrapolate between conditional text predictions and unconditional outputs to sharpen prompt alignment.

latent-diffusion-models-stable-diffusion.idea: Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) execute iterative diffusion and denoising operations within the compressed latent space of a pre-trained autoencoder.
latent-diffusion-models-stable-diffusion.why: Computing multi-step diffusion in raw high-resolution pixel space consumes excessive processing time and memory. Compact latent manifolds preserve perceptual detail while accelerating generation.
latent-diffusion-models-stable-diffusion.example: Stable Diffusion pipelines denoise compressed latent representations across diffusion steps before decoding latents into final images.

variational-autoencoders-vae.idea: Variational Autoencoders map input data into smooth continuous latent distributions via the reparameterization trick to support probabilistic reconstruction and sampling.
variational-autoencoders-vae.why: Standard autoencoder representations develop irregular latent gaps that disrupt generative decoding. Imposing prior distribution penalties enforces continuous, interpolatable latent spaces.
variational-autoencoders-vae.example: Deep autoencoders sample latent vectors from smooth continuous distributions to reconstruct images with trained decoders.

vector-quantized-vae-vqvae.idea: Vector Quantized VAE (VQ-VAE) architectures map continuous encoder representations to nearest entries in a learned discrete codebook.
vector-quantized-vae-vqvae.why: Continuous latent variables frequently experience posterior collapse when paired with expressive decoders. Discrete codebook quantization maintains distinct symbolic bottlenecks without collapse.
vector-quantized-vae-vqvae.example: Neural audio encoders quantize continuous acoustic features into discrete codebook sequences for autoregressive sequence modeling.

adamw-decoupled-weight-decay.idea: AdamW decouples weight decay from adaptive gradient momentum updates, ensuring uniform regularization across parameters regardless of historical gradient scale.
adamw-decoupled-weight-decay.why: Coupling L2 penalties with adaptive moving averages diminishes regularization on weights with infrequent large gradients. Direct parameter decay maintains consistent regularization strength.
adamw-decoupled-weight-decay.example: Optimization routines apply decoupled weight decay directly to model parameters after computing adaptive Adam step directions.

rms-normalization-and-layer-norm.idea: Root Mean Square Normalization (RMSNorm) scales layer input activations by their root mean square alone, omitting the mean centering operation in LayerNorm.
rms-normalization-and-layer-norm.why: Calculating mean statistics requires additional reduction passes across tensor dimensions without yielding noticeable stability improvements. Normalizing by root mean square preserves scaling stability.
rms-normalization-and-layer-norm.example: Transformer layers divide incoming token activation vectors by root mean square values to stabilize layer inputs.

cosine-annealing-warmup-schedules.idea: Cosine annealing with warmup schedules linearly ramps learning rates during initial iterations before gradually decaying them following a cosine curve.
cosine-annealing-warmup-schedules.why: Elevated learning rates during early optimization can destabilize randomly initialized parameters. Gradual warming followed by smooth cosine decay supports stable training convergence.
cosine-annealing-warmup-schedules.example: Training loops scale optimizer learning rates upward over initial steps before decreasing values along cosine curves.

gradient-accumulation-and-mixed-precisio.idea: FP16 and BF16 mixed precision training accelerates neural computation and halves GPU memory by running tensor contractions in half precision while preserving master weights.
gradient-accumulation-and-mixed-precisio.why: Full precision storage underutilizes modern tensor acceleration cores and limits batch sizes. Half-precision computation conserves bandwidth while master copies prevent precision loss.
gradient-accumulation-and-mixed-precisio.example: Automatic mixed precision contexts cast forward activations into Bfloat16 while storing master parameter copies in full precision.

proximal-policy-optimization-ppo.idea: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) maximizes a clipped surrogate objective function to prevent policy parameter updates from straying excessively from previous iterations.
proximal-policy-optimization-ppo.why: Unconstrained policy gradient steps can cause policy collapse when updates move into detrimental performance regions. Clipping probability ratios enforces bounded, stable updates.
proximal-policy-optimization-ppo.example: Reinforcement learning agents clip surrogate policy objective ratios to stabilize actor updates during environmental interaction.

monte-carlo-tree-search-alphazero.idea: Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) combines neural policy and value evaluations with heuristic search trees to navigate complex decision spaces.
monte-carlo-tree-search-alphazero.why: Exhaustive evaluation of combinatorial game branches exceeds computational budgets. Heuristic selection using confidence bounds focuses exploration along promising trajectory branches.
monte-carlo-tree-search-alphazero.example: AlphaZero systems evaluate board positions by running simulated rollouts and selecting moves using tree search bounds.

deep-q-networks-dqn-experience-replay.idea: Deep Q-Networks (DQN) combine deep neural networks with experience replay buffers to approximate action-value functions during reinforcement learning.
deep-q-networks-dqn-experience-replay.why: Sequential state transitions introduce temporal correlation and non-stationary training distributions. Sampling transition batches randomly from replay buffers stabilizes optimization.
deep-q-networks-dqn-experience-replay.example: DQN controllers sample batches of past environmental transitions from replay buffers to calculate temporal difference errors.

clip-contrastive-language-image-pretrain.idea: CLIP pre-trains image and text encoders simultaneously on matched pairs using contrastive language-image pretraining to build a shared multimodal embedding space.
clip-contrastive-language-image-pretrain.why: Standard vision classifiers depend on fixed categorical labels that do not transfer across novel domains. Multimodal contrastive objectives align visual concepts with natural language.
clip-contrastive-language-image-pretrain.example: Contrastive vision models measure cosine similarity between visual embeddings and text labels to classify images without fine-tuning.

llava-visual-instruction-tuning.idea: LLaVA connects a visual feature encoder with a language model decoder via a projection layer, enabling conversational visual instruction following.
llava-visual-instruction-tuning.why: Standalone text decoders cannot process raw image inputs directly. Aligning visual features into language embedding spaces enables models to reason over images.
llava-visual-instruction-tuning.example: Multimodal dialogue models project visual feature tokens into language decoders to answer questions regarding uploaded images.

neural-radiance-fields-nerf.idea: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) represent continuous volumetric scenes as coordinate functions parameterized by neural networks to render novel 3D views.
neural-radiance-fields-nerf.why: Traditional polygonal meshes struggle to capture complex geometries and specular lighting effects accurately. Continuous radiance functions optimize volumetric densities and colors directly.
neural-radiance-fields-nerf.example: Volumetric rendering functions query spatial coordinates along camera rays to synthesize novel camera views from photographs.

3d-gaussian-splatting.idea: 3D Gaussian Splatting for real-time radiance field rendering represents scenes using anisotropic 3D Gaussians optimized via differentiable tile rasterization.
3d-gaussian-splatting.why: Continuous volumetric ray marching requires dense sampling passes that inhibit real-time frame rates. Differentiable splatting rasterizes explicit primitives with hardware efficiency.
3d-gaussian-splatting.example: Real-time graphics renderers project anisotropic Gaussian primitives onto screen tiles to display complex reconstructed environments.

knowledge-distillation-teacher-student.idea: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into compact student models by training student architectures on softened logit distributions.
knowledge-distillation-teacher-student.why: Raw target labels omit information regarding relative class similarities captured by large architectures. Soft probability distributions convey nuanced relationships that guide compact models.
knowledge-distillation-teacher-student.example: Compact student transformers train on softened logit distributions produced by larger teacher models to retain task performance.

word2vec-skipgram-negative-sampling.idea: Word2Vec skip-gram with negative sampling (SGNS) trains shallow networks to maximize context word probabilities while discriminating against negative noise samples.
word2vec-skipgram-negative-sampling.why: Full vocabulary softmax calculations become computationally prohibitive over massive corpora. Negative sampling replaces expensive normalizations with binary classification tasks.
word2vec-skipgram-negative-sampling.example: Embedding models update target word vectors to predict nearby context tokens while distinguishing randomly sampled noise words.

contrastive-representation-learning-simc.idea: SimCLR learns visual representations by maximizing agreement between differently augmented views of images using contrastive loss objectives without human labels.
contrastive-representation-learning-simc.why: Supervised feature training requires extensive manual annotation across domain tasks. Self-supervised contrastive learning extracts generalizable visual representations from raw image datasets.
contrastive-representation-learning-simc.example: Self-supervised vision pipelines apply data augmentations to input images and pull matching representation views together in feature space.

masked-autoencoders-mae.idea: Masked Autoencoders (MAE) are scalable vision learners that mask high proportions of image patches and reconstruct missing pixels using asymmetric autoencoders.
masked-autoencoders-mae.why: Processing entire visual frames creates redundant spatial computation during pre-training. Masking high patch fractions accelerates encoder training and discourages shallow texture memorization.
masked-autoencoders-mae.example: Vision transformer encoders process visible image patches while lightweight decoders reconstruct masked pixel regions during pre-training.

chinchilla-compute-optimal-scaling-laws.idea: Chinchilla scaling laws for compute-optimal pre-training show that model parameters and training dataset tokens should scale proportionally given fixed budgets.
chinchilla-compute-optimal-scaling-laws.why: Allocating available compute primarily to model size produces under-trained parameter representations. Balancing parameter counts with token volume optimizes performance per unit computation.
chinchilla-compute-optimal-scaling-laws.example: Pre-training budgets allocate resources equally between scaling model parameter counts and expanding dataset token volume.

emergent-abilities-and-grokking.idea: Grokking and phase transitions in generalization describe sudden transitions where overparameterized neural networks achieve generalization long after memorizing training data.
emergent-abilities-and-grokking.why: Standard training assumptions view generalization as occurring concurrently with loss minimization. Prolonged training can induce structural circuit formation well after loss reaches zero.
emergent-abilities-and-grokking.example: Neural networks trained on modular arithmetic maintain memorized weights before undergoing sharp phase transitions toward generalization.

mechanistic-interpretability-induction-h.idea: Mechanistic interpretability reverse-engineers trained neural networks into discrete computational circuits such as induction heads that perform in-context sequence copying.
mechanistic-interpretability-induction-h.why: Treating neural models as inscrutable black boxes restricts system debugging and safety verification. Isolating discrete internal circuits reveals concrete computational mechanisms.
mechanistic-interpretability-induction-h.example: Interpretability tools trace attention head activations across transformer layers to identify circuits responsible for in-context pattern copying.

react-reasoning-and-acting.idea: ReAct synergizes reasoning and acting in language models by interleaving verbal chain-of-thought traces with tool actions to solve interactive tasks.
react-reasoning-and-acting.why: Internal reasoning without external actions risks factual hallucination, whereas invoking external tools without planning causes erratic behavior. Alternating traces enables grounded problem solving.
react-reasoning-and-acting.example: Autonomous agent loops produce explicit reasoning thoughts before calling search APIs and observing return values to update plans.

tree-of-thoughts-prompting.idea: Tree of Thoughts (ToT) problem solving expands reasoning into branching trees of intermediate thoughts, enabling systematic evaluation and backtracking across paths.
tree-of-thoughts-prompting.why: Linear generation commits to preliminary choices without opportunity to rectify flawed deductions. Tree exploration allows models to assess alternatives and abandon unpromising paths.
tree-of-thoughts-prompting.example: Problem solving prompts generate candidate thought branches and prune unfeasible options using tree search algorithms.
